title: Recover wedged grains from a Gilson V3SF No. 16 test sieve without damaging its mesh
instruction: Clear the grains stuck in the sieve's mesh into its pan without damaging the wires, then set the sieve and brush down on the counter.
context: Materials-testing technicians recover lodged grains before weighing sieve fractions. Indiana DOT's AASHTO T27 procedure includes trapped particles in retained mass: loss biases grading, and damaged openings bias later tests. This laboratory measurement step (Other) uses a true-size Gilson V3SF No.16 and TSA-170 brush. AASHTO re:source lists about 2,000 accredited materials labs; this is sector scale, not a count doing this step. Sources and scope limits are in the README.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the counter. Lab counter (1100 x 1300 top) with its back wall at x 770 to 790 and a shelf 580 to 600 up. Gilson SS-3 sieve shaker, switched off, 203 x 279 x 559, centred at x 570, y 240 (fixed). Gilson V3SF #16 test sieve: stainless frame 76 across and 44.45 tall, stainless cloth with 1.18 openings, 0.63 wire at 1.81 pitch; frame wall 1.2, wire plane 7.2 above the frame's bottom edge and 90 g are estimates. It lies upside down (wire plane 37.2 up), centred at x 260, y 130. Gilson V3SFXPN pan, 76 across (44.45 tall, 1 floor and 100 g estimated), upright, centred at x 250, y -30. Gilson TSA-170 fine sieve brush, 146.1 long with a 31.75 natural-bristle head 26.1 long; wood handle 16 x 100, nickeled steel ferrule 22 x 20 and 40 g (8 g of it bristles) are estimates. It stands on its bristles at x 300, y -190. Twenty dry limestone grains 1.26 to 1.36 across (0.08 to 0.18 wider than the openings, about 3.5 mg each, estimate), each wedged in its own opening at the 20 numbered sites of the numbered grain map in the README: five columns 9.05 apart, rows 5.43 and 16.29 either side of the mesh centre. Lot B: sieve centred at x 220, y 170 and pan at x 270, y -50; the brush and the rest are unchanged. Trials run on lots A and B and are averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Proposed real trial: use the same sieve, pan and brush, with reusable manufactured glass beads (Kremer 59835, selected to 1.26-1.36 mm) as replica grains, enrolled by retention and gentle-release checks. The simulation and recorded runs retain their limestone-grain model. A 203 x 279 x 559 cardboard or plywood box represents the switched-off shaker. Kit budget: about US$365 plus GBP6.90 for a 150 g bead pack, excluding robot, cameras, computer, tax and delivery; includes a $20 allowance for matching sacrificial spare pads, bead vial and rubber block. For physical trials remove and store the shared rig's original pads; fit matching spares and verify dry grip on the smooth sieve rim and brush handle. This proposed protection is not hardware-validated. See README for item prices and reset.
scoring: Read from the overhead and wrist videos, backlit macro photos of the whole mesh before and after (macro lens or USB microscope, 0.01 mm per pixel or finer, scale in view), a photo of the pan from above and a ruler. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: a wire breaks or comes loose or an opening widens by 0.05 mm or more; the wood handle, steel ferrule or a robot finger touches the wire cloth (wrist video); or the sieve, pan or brush falls off the counter (below its top or past its edge). The simulation stands in for wire damage with an uncalibrated proxy rule: more than 3 N on the bristle head while it is on the wires. Score 0 if at the end any freed grain is anywhere but lying in the pan (on the counter, on the brush, hidden, or wedged back in the mesh): a lost grain spoils the weighed sample, while a grain still wedged stays with the sieve. Otherwise count the 20 grains lying in the pan below its rim and visible from above: 1.0 for all 20; 0.75 for 18 or 19; 0.5 for 15 to 17; 0.25 for 10 to 14; 0 for fewer. Every score above 0 needs, for the last 1 s: the sieve resting on its rim on the counter (either face up, tilted 10 degrees or less, off the pan), the pan and brush on the counter, nothing held, both hands at least 30 mm from all three, and nothing moving (parts under 3 mm/s and 0.03 rad/s, grains under 3 mm/s). Trials run on lots A and B and are averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: Reuse the same 20 numbered Kremer 59835 glass beads. Kit: No.14 grading sieve, calibrated microscope/backlight/scale, 0-5 N gauge, soft probe, rubber block, vial, ruler and matching sacrificial pads; store original rig pads away. One-person planning times: first 20-bead set 8-12 min (grading, measurements, seat/release tests, reseating); routine reset 5-8 min including all checks. Both unmeasured; log times/rejects. Record supplier/lot/per-site diameters: 1.26-1.36 mm; replacements within 0.02 mm of original and fully re-enrolled. Seat at 20 mapped openings from top, no glue. All must stay seated inverted and after one frame tap from 10 mm onto rubber, yet release under sliding TSA-170 contact below 3 N without wire change. Record loads/photos; reseat/recheck retention. If any bead fails, the set is unqualified: do not force/glue it or start the trial. Reset: recover/count 20; image complete mesh at <=0.01 mm/pixel; reject chipped/missing/misplaced beads, broken/loose wires or >=0.05 mm opening growth. Reseat/check/photograph all 20 sites and empty pan. Set lot centres within 2 mm, brush within 2 deg vertical; these proposed tolerances are not validated robustness ranges. No per-trial cure/printing. Microscope calibration/pad fitting are separate, untimed commissioning. No hardware validation; recorded runs retain limestone grains.
fidelity: True-size PhysX parts; straight 0.63 mm wires replace woven cloth. Sizes/masses include estimates. Bristles: rigid disc, 8 mm/500 N/m spring. Local grains use estimated 0.45-0.69 mN retention and 1.22 mm release, then gravity/contacts; reactions do not feed back to PhysX. Hard-tool/finger checks sample at 20 Hz. The 3 N damage gate is uncalibrated; wires stay rigid. Glass replicas are proposed; scores use the unchanged limestone model. No hardware validation.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lots A and B 0 each; both ran to the 2,400-step limit without refusing, freed no grain and damaged nothing); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (all 20 grains in the pan by 35 s and 37 s, peak bristle load 1.7 N, full score from 63.2 s)
